new.title: With the ordered pair and triple witness conditions, selecting a row after free column preprocessing needs 2n−1 AND/OR gates
new.statement:
∀ (n m p : Nat) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (code : Fin m → Fin p → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  2 ≤ n →
  (∀ u v : Fin n, u ≠ v →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) →
  (∀ u v w : Fin n, u ≠ v → u ≠ w → v ≠ w →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  (∀ (u : Fin n) (c : Fin m),
    C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (i = u)) ++ List.ofFn (code c)) = G u c) →
  2 * n - 1 ≤ C.size
new.unlocks: bounds the remaining row-selector gates when column preprocessing is free
new.context: Fix the column code when comparing rows. With two incomparable rows both raw inputs matter and neither can feed the output directly. One shared initial gate treats them alike, so three gates are needed. Turning off a row saves two gates if it has two readers or its sole reader is AND. Otherwise count the private row ORs. Domination excludes a shared sole OR reader. A common column missed by a third excludes a shared sole AND reader. Charge two reader slots per row OR. The matching ceiling uses n free column predicates, n ANDs and n−1 ORs.

changed.title: A fixed 32 by 32 bipartite graph given by its table: some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 128 gates is right whenever one row and one column are on
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 128 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 32 => (([0xf2bc7573, 0x59092a9d, 0xc443c8c2, 0x1d58483a, 0x1b7982bb, 0xa8882290, 0x74d0fd25, 0x00041402, 0x6879a8a5, 0xd65a6f1a, 0x7455fba3, 0x24508c1a, 0x3050a010, 0x68658ad5, 0x10a00735, 0x5e55690e, 0x6ab804a4, 0x00b01458, 0xf447af40, 0x00b07351, 0xa88c2290, 0x40d9d7bc, 0x40241486, 0x54058082, 0x6891afb9, 0x50ddf79e, 0x553080be, 0x28c180f8, 0x6ac8ae9e, 0xa6860e80, 0x20508c18, 0x10f01050] : List ℕ).getD u.val 0).testBit v.val) C
changed.unlocks: a circuit under the count we hold for this graph; how low the count goes is what we want to learn
changed.context: We hold 255 gates for this table: one AND of two ORs for each key, all ORed. Only the gate list is checked. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
changed.sketch: Row u of the table, as a hex number, is entry u of the list in the statement; bit v is set when row u is joined to column v. The table comes from a keyed mixing rule of ours (k = 5). We hold 255 gates: for each key, the OR of its rows AND the OR of its columns, all ORed; sharing those ORs between keys brings ours to 225 (computed). Answer with a gate list; it is checked by one evaluation per promise input (1024). Any method. A prover can use represents_of_pcols in lean/PEqualNP/Library/Helpers/PromiseCol.lean. At 128, four gates a side-vertex: truth unknown to us.

changed.title: The 8 by 8 graph with mask 8080454460742251720 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR circuit of fan-in two with at most 24 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 8 => (8080454460742251720 : ℕ).testBit (8 * u.val + v.val)) 24
changed.unlocks: the least cost of one dense 8 by 8 graph with no equal lines, approached from above
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of this size; this is a search. Our circuit is the row star with shared ORs; pairs of columns that occur together in several rows may save gates.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 3937373 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 10 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 10 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => (3937373 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: Whether a NOT gate pays under a checked AND/OR floor of 11 on this side-5 graph, by leaving its classes of equal rows or columns unread.
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of 10 gates; this is a search. This graph has a class of 2 equal columns, which a circuit with NOT gates may leave unread. Give a gate list of AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two, at most 10 gates, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. The graph needs at least 11 AND/OR gates by a checked floor row (search 'mask 3937373'). An exhausted search is a report, not a proof.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 3 by 4 bipartite graph with mask 363 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 7 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 3) (v : Fin 4) => (363 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) 7
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 3 by 4 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 8 AND/OR gates for this graph that shares nothing; we hold none of 7; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 6 (on paper), a gap of 2. The checked twin merge reduces a square graph to a rectangular quotient, and we hold no table off the square beyond 2 by 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 2 left, 3 to 6 right, gate j writes wire 7 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 12 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: At most 2+e private rows have distinct profiles outside a narrow column set in an AND/OR region with e at most one entry wire
changed.statement:
∀ (n m d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (R : Finset (Fin n)) (B : Finset (Fin m)) (region entry : Finset ℕ) (top : ℕ),
  let raw := n + m
  let sources := R.image (fun sourceRow => sourceRow.val) ∪ B.image (fun sourceCol => n + sourceCol.val)
  let inside := fun (w : ℕ) => raw ≤ w ∧ w - raw ∈ region
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  (∀ firstRow secondRow : Fin n, firstRow ≠ secondRow → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun col => G firstRow col ≠ G secondRow col)).card) →
  (∀ firstCol secondCol : Fin m, firstCol ≠ secondCol → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun row => G row firstCol ≠ G row secondCol)).card) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack raw C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → region ⊆ Finset.range C.size → top ∈ region →
  entry.card ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ entry, w < raw + top ∧ w ∉ sources ∧ ¬ inside w) →
  (∀ k ∈ region,
    ((gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
     (gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
    ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs, w ∈ sources ∨ inside w ∨ w ∈ entry) →
  (∀ k < C.size, k ∉ region → ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs,
    w ∉ sources ∧ (inside w → w = raw + top)) →
  C.output ∉ sources → (inside C.output → C.output = raw + top) →
  (B.card < d → R.card ≤ 2 + entry.card) ∧ (R.card < d → B.card ≤ 2 + entry.card)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of private rows or columns whose profiles differ outside a small opposite set
changed.context: Fix an active outside column and vary the active private row. Until the top, outside gates cannot read a private signal, so the entry value depends only on the column. In the region each row induces a monotone unary truth table on that bit, either zero, identity or one. Without an entry there are two constant tables. Equal tables give identical outputs on every outside column, since only the top leaves the region. Fewer than d private columns cannot hide d disagreements. Count the types and exchange sides. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a bound on private inputs.

changed.title: Exact maximum size of a sparse rectangle from its exterior profiles and a three-corner condition
changed.unlocks: gives the exact rectangle size used at two and three exterior profiles in the sparse circuit argument
changed.context: Edge closure gives stars. Full edge lines bound the opposite side by d. Empty-profile centers use disjoint pairs of leaves. With one empty-profile side, a largest nonempty class of h≥2 rows uses h other neighbors. For nonedge closure, two nonneighbors of one row force at most one row outside its class. With three core rows, at most one column lies outside that nonneighbor set. A matching attains 2dt. For the other bound group d copies of the t−1 labels cyclically into pairs, with one triple for odd total, then add the transpose. Gate-price companions cannot exist for this vertex count.
